name: io.github.asachs01/lectio-api
title: Lectio API
description: Lectionary readings (RCL, BCP Daily Office, Catholic) and liturgical calendar tools.

tools.name: get_readings
tools.description: Fetch Sunday or daily lectionary readings. Pass date (YYYY-MM-DD) for a single day, omit date for today in tz, or pass startDate and endDate for a range. Shared params: tradition, tz. Use this when the user wants scripture citations or Daily Office readings. Do not use it to list seasons, look up a feast by name, or get the cycle letter — use get_calendar or search_lectionary.

date.description: Single civil date (YYYY-MM-DD). Omit to get today in tz. Do not combine with startDate/endDate.

startDate.description: Start of a date range (YYYY-MM-DD). Requires endDate.

endDate.description: End of a date range (YYYY-MM-DD). Requires startDate.

tradition.description: Lectionary tradition. rcl (default) is the Revised Common Lectionary; catholic is the Roman Catholic lectionary; episcopal is RCL Sundays with BCP Daily Office weekdays; bcp is the BCP Daily Office only.

tz.description: IANA time zone used to decide "today" and the current civil year, e.g. America/New_York, America/Chicago, Europe/London. Defaults to America/New_York (or LECTIO_TIMEZONE). Takes effect once the API tz parameter is deployed.

tools.name: get_calendar
tools.description: Fetch liturgical calendar data, grouped by focus: current (today's season and cycle, uses tz); year (civil-year overview, requires year); seasons (season date ranges, requires year); special_days (all named holy days in a year); upcoming (holy days from today or date forward); feast (look up a feast by feastName); context (factual season, readings, and generic season theme labels for a date — not generated commentary). Shared params: tradition, tz, date, year. Use search_lectionary if the user names a season rather than a date.

focus.description: Defaults to current. year and seasons require year; feast requires feastName; context requires date.

date.description: Civil date for focus=context, or the "from" date for focus=upcoming.

feastName.description: Feast or holy day name, required when focus is feast. Examples: Christmas, Ash Wednesday, Trinity Sunday.

tradition.description: Lectionary tradition. rcl (default) is the Revised Common Lectionary; catholic is the Roman Catholic lectionary; episcopal is RCL Sundays with BCP Daily Office weekdays; bcp is the BCP Daily Office only.

tz.description: IANA time zone used to decide "today" and the current civil year, e.g. America/New_York, America/Chicago, Europe/London. Defaults to America/New_York (or LECTIO_TIMEZONE). Takes effect once the API tz parameter is deployed.

tools.name: list_traditions
tools.description: List supported lectionary traditions and their metadata (rcl, catholic, episcopal, bcp), or pass id to fetch a single tradition. Use this to discover valid tradition values before calling get_readings or get_calendar. This does not return readings or calendar dates.

id.description: Tradition id to fetch a single record. Omit to list all.

tools.name: search_lectionary
tools.description: Search readings when the user names a liturgical season (Advent, Lent, Easter, Ordinary Time) or a feast / holy day (Christmas, Ash Wednesday, Trinity Sunday), not a calendar date. For a known YYYY-MM-DD date or a date range, use get_readings instead. There is no scripture-reference search. searchType=date_range is accepted for one release as a deprecated alias of get_readings with startDate and endDate.

searchType.description: season requires season; feast requires feastName. date_range is deprecated — use get_readings with startDate and endDate.

season.description: Season name, e.g. Advent, Lent, Easter, Ordinary Time.

feastName.description: Feast or holy day name, e.g. Christmas, Ash Wednesday, Trinity Sunday.

startDate.description: Deprecated. Use get_readings with startDate and endDate.

endDate.description: Deprecated. Use get_readings with startDate and endDate.

year.description: Civil year to search. Defaults to the current year in tz, then the previous year if there is no match.

tradition.description: Lectionary tradition. rcl (default) is the Revised Common Lectionary; catholic is the Roman Catholic lectionary; episcopal is RCL Sundays with BCP Daily Office weekdays; bcp is the BCP Daily Office only.

tz.description: IANA time zone used to decide "today" and the current civil year, e.g. America/New_York, America/Chicago, Europe/London. Defaults to America/New_York (or LECTIO_TIMEZONE). Takes effect once the API tz parameter is deployed.

tools.name: explore_calendar
tools.description: This tool name is deprecated and will be removed in the next major release. Prefer the canonical name. Use get_calendar with the same focus values (current, year, seasons, special_days). Additional focuses upcoming, feast, and context are only documented on get_calendar.

focus.description: Same values as get_calendar. year and seasons require year.

tradition.description: Lectionary tradition. rcl (default) is the Revised Common Lectionary; catholic is the Roman Catholic lectionary; episcopal is RCL Sundays with BCP Daily Office weekdays; bcp is the BCP Daily Office only.

tz.description: IANA time zone used to decide "today" and the current civil year, e.g. America/New_York, America/Chicago, Europe/London. Defaults to America/New_York (or LECTIO_TIMEZONE). Takes effect once the API tz parameter is deployed.

date.description: Civil calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format (not a UTC timestamp).

tools.name: analyze_liturgical_context
tools.description: This tool name is deprecated and will be removed in the next major release. Prefer the canonical name. Use get_calendar with focus=context and a date. This alias no longer invents theological connections, significance, or applications; it returns factual season and reading data plus generic season theme labels.

tradition.description: Lectionary tradition. rcl (default) is the Revised Common Lectionary; catholic is the Roman Catholic lectionary; episcopal is RCL Sundays with BCP Daily Office weekdays; bcp is the BCP Daily Office only.

depth.description: Ignored. Kept so existing callers do not fail validation. Commentary is never generated.
